name: danish-monarchs

description.en: The 22 monarchs of Denmark from Christian I, the first king of the House of Oldenburg (1448), to Frederik X, king since 14 January 2024, as of 4 October 2026. Front: the monarch's regnal name in English and Swedish; back: the years of the reign, counted from accession to death, deposition or abdication, with the royal house (Oldenburg or Glücksburg) and a short fact in a note. Taken from Wikidata (one note from the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica) and checked against the Danish Royal House's list of monarchs (kongehuset.dk), Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon, Nationalencyklopedin and the Swedish Wikipedia.
description.sv: Danmarks 22 regenter från Kristian I, den förste kungen av huset Oldenburg (1448), till Frederik X, kung sedan den 14 januari 2024, per den 4 oktober 2026. Framsida: regentens namn på engelska och svenska; baksida: regeringsåren, räknade från trontillträdet till regentens död, avsättning eller abdikation, med kungahuset (Oldenburg eller Glücksburg) och en kort upplysning i en anteckning. Uppgifterna är hämtade från Wikidata (en anteckning från Encyclopædia Britannica 1911, som är fri från upphovsrätt) och kontrollerade mot det danska kungahusets regentlängd (kongehuset.dk), Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon, Nationalencyklopedin och svenskspråkiga Wikipedia.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
Finding the position: the Wikidata search API (query 6) returned Q18341329 "Monarch of Denmark" ("monarchical head of state of the Kingdom of Denmark").

Selection and reign years: query 1 fetched as CSV from the Wikidata Query Service every non-deprecated P39 (position held) statement whose value is Q18341329, with its P580 (start time), P582 (end time), P1365 (replaces) and P1366 (replaced by) qualifiers, its rank, the holder's P53 (family) with the family's English and Swedish labels, and the holder's English and Swedish labels. The result runs from legendary kings to the present. The holders whose statement starts in 1448 or later are 22 people, Christian I (start 1448-10-07) to Frederik X (start 2024-01-14, preferred rank, no end time), each with one statement, linked into one unbroken chain by the replaces/replaced-by qualifiers; they became the cards. The back of each card is the year of P580 and the year of P582, joined by an en dash, and "2024–" for Frederik X, whose reign continues. No card's years come from anywhere else; the other sources only confirmed or differed (see quality control).

Note facts: query 2 fetched for the 22 statements the end-cause qualifier (P1534), the holder's father (P22) and date of birth (P569); query 2b Frederik X's mother (P25); query 3 the properties of the House of Oldenburg (Q155594), the House of Glücksburg (Q155616) and its Danish branch item (Q111201485); query 4 the holders' other positions (P39 Monarch of Sweden, Monarch of Norway) with their start and end and the date of death (P570). Every note fact but one is a Wikidata statement or follows directly from two of them (that Christian II was Frederick I's nephew: Frederick I and Hans are both sons of Christian I, Christian II is the son of Hans; that the throne was vacant from 1533 to 1534: Frederick I's statement ends in April 1533 and Christian III's starts in July 1534; that Christian IV was ten at his accession: born 1577-04-22, king from 1588-04-14). The notes are the compiler's own wording, written directly in English and in Swedish. The exception is Christian IV's coming of age in 1596, which Wikidata does not hold (query 4b found no P793 significant-event statement on Q153586): it comes from the public-domain 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica article "Christian IV." by Robert Nisbet Bain on Wikisource (query 15 fetched the article pages, which only transclude the scanned pages; query 16 the transcribed page that holds the article's opening, "attaining his majority on the 17th of August 1596"; query 17 its licence box), and Lex ("Først 8 år senere i 1596 blev han kronet til dansk-norsk konge og dermed regent") and Nationalencyklopedin ("dröjde det till 1596 innan han blev myndig och kröntes") confirm it. The years that the Royal House's list gives where it differs from the cards (Hans, Christian III, Christian IV) are recorded in those cards' evidence and in quality control, not in the notes.

Names: the Wikidata API (query 5) fetched the English, Swedish, Danish and multilingual labels and aliases and the English, Swedish and Danish Wikipedia sitelinks of the 22 monarchs and the three house items. English fronts: the Wikidata English label or alias without "of Denmark". The Christians are Christian I–X. The Fredericks follow one rule: Frederick (the English form) for the seven kings of the House of Oldenburg, Frederik (the Danish form) for the three of the House of Glücksburg, as Wikidata's English labels and aliases have them (aliases "Frederick I" … "Frederick VII"; labels "Frederik VIII of Denmark", "Frederik IX of Denmark", "Frederik X of Denmark"), and as the English Wikipedia titles do except for Frederick VIII. King Hans is "Hans" in English too: his Wikidata English label is "John, King of Denmark" but his English alias, the English Wikipedia title ("Hans, King of Denmark") and the Royal House's English page all use Hans. Swedish fronts: the Wikidata Swedish label or alias without "av Danmark": Kristian I–X, Fredrik I–IX, Hans, Margrethe II and Frederik X. That is also how the Swedish Wikipedia list names every one of them, and Nationalencyklopedin writes Kristian IV, V, VI, VIII, IX, X, Fredrik IV, Fredrik IX ("danska Frederik IX"), Margrethe II and Frederik X (queries 12–13): Swedish keeps the Swedish forms Kristian and Fredrik for the historical kings but the Danish form Frederik for the present king, so the deck does too. The house names in the notes are the Wikidata labels: House of Oldenburg / Huset Oldenburg (Q155594), House of Glücksburg (Q155616) / huset Glücksburg (Q111201485, capitalised at the start of a note).

Official check: the Danish Royal House's English page "The Royal Lineage" was downloaded with curl and its text extracted with a small HTML-to-text script (query 7). It gives each monarch's years twice, in the entry heading and in the timeline; every card's years were compared with both. They agree for 19 monarchs; for Hans (1482–1513), Christian III (timeline 1534–1559, heading 1536–1559, and an interregnum 1533–1536) and Christian IV (1588/1596–1648) the page differs, see quality control. Its timeline shows "Frederik X — Since 2024", which together with Wikidata (no end time), Lex ("2024-", article last changed 15 September 2026) and Nationalencyklopedin ("kung av Danmark sedan 2024") confirms that Frederik X still reigned on 4 October 2026.

Independent check: the article "kongerækken i Danmark" in Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon (query 8) gives the years of every reign; it agrees with every card, including Hans 1481–1513, Christian III 1534–1559 (interregnum 1533–1534) and Christian IV 1588–1648. Its licence terms were read (query 9). The Swedish Wikipedia "Lista över Danmarks regenter" (query 10, wikitext of revision 59658833 through the MediaWiki API; query 11 for the licence footer) gives the Swedish name and the accession and end date of every reign; every card agrees with it. The comparison was done by reading the extracted texts side by side with the Wikidata CSV; each card's evidence quotes the row of each source.

Dossier: the script make_dossier.py (a working script, not published; everything it produced is in this dossier) wrote the first version of the cards. It holds a table with one row per monarch in order of accession: the card id, the English and Swedish fronts and the Wikidata label or alias each is checked against (chosen by the rule in the fifth step), the back (the P580 and P582 years read from q1.csv), and the readings of Lex, the Royal House's page and the Swedish Wikipedia typed in from the extracted texts; a second table holds each card's notes, written by hand from the facts listed in the fourth step, with the Wikidata statements they rely on, and a third the Nationalencyklopedin quotes. For each row it read the statement's start, end, rank and P53 houses from q1.csv and the label-or-alias kind and the sitelinks from names.json, and wrote the card, its evidence (the "says" texts) and its Wikidata checks. Later changes were made to the dossier directly and are logged under quality control. The 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource (query 15) was first considered for the note facts and set aside because its article pages only transclude scanned pages; in review round 3 the transcribed page for Christian IV was read (query 16) and supplies one note fact (fourth step).

Machine checks: every card carries Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: P39 = Q18341329 (the person held the position), P53 = the house named in the note (House of Oldenburg Q155594, House of Glücksburg Q155616 or its Danish branch item Q111201485, whichever the item holds), the English and Swedish front text as a label or alias (with the disambiguator where the front drops one), the house labels, and every statement a note relies on (P22, P25, P39 Monarch of Sweden / Norway, P569 and P570 years, P361, P53 of the neighbouring monarch, the aliases Kristian Tyrann, Johan II, Christian Frederick and Kristian Fredrik). The reign years are qualifiers, which the builder's checks cannot read; they rest on query 1 and the comparison in the sixth and seventh steps and are quoted in each card's evidence. The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
selection: Every monarch of Denmark from Christian I, elected in 1448 as the first king of the House of Oldenburg, to Frederik X, king since 14 January 2024 and still reigning on 4 October 2026: 22 cards, among them one queen regnant, Margrethe II. A reign is counted from accession (succession on the predecessor's death or abdication, or election) to the monarch's death, deposition or abdication; coronations are not used (so Christian IV counts from 1588, not 1596), and only years are given. The throne was vacant between Frederick I's death in 1533 and Christian III's election in 1534; that interregnum gets no card. Left out: the monarchs before 1448 (Christopher of Bavaria and earlier, of other houses and, before Gorm the Old, of uncertain dates), regents who were not monarchs (Frederick VI as regent for his father from 1784 is not counted before 1808), and Christian VIII's and others' reigns in Norway and Sweden as cards of their own (they appear in notes). The years of the reigns of Hans, Christian III and Christian IV differ in some lists; the cards follow Wikidata, Lex and the Swedish Wikipedia, and the Royal House's differing figures are recorded in those cards' evidence.
licensing: The content sources are Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0, and the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource, which is in the public domain (published before 1931; its article on Christian IV is by Robert Nisbet Bain, who died in 1909). The selection of monarchs, the reign years, the English and Swedish names, the royal houses and every fact in the notes come from Wikidata, except Christian IV's coming of age in 1596, which comes from the Britannica article, so the deck is CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. The Danish Royal House's website (all rights reserved), Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon (copyright, restricted reuse), Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts that the content sources gave, and no wording, table layout, name form, selection or fact was taken from them. The Royal House's differing years for three reigns are recorded only in the evidence and the quality-control log, where short quotations document the check. The selection is the complete line of Danish monarchs since 1448, which every list shares because it is the complete set, not a choice taken from any one list. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording of facts.

queries.purpose: 1. Every P39 statement for Monarch of Denmark with start, end, replaces, replaced by, rank, house and labels (sh <scratch>/run.sh q1, which runs: curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq https://query.wikidata.org/sparql > q1.csv)
2. End cause, father and date of birth of the 22 monarchs (sh <scratch>/run.sh q2)
2b. Frederik X's mother (P25), added in review round 3 because query 2 did not fetch it (sh <scratch>/run.sh q2b)
3. Properties of the House of Oldenburg, the House of Glücksburg and its Danish branch item (sh <scratch>/run.sh q3)
4. Other positions held (Sweden, Norway) and dates of death of nine of the monarchs (sh <scratch>/run.sh q4)
4b. Significant events (P793) on Christian IV's item, looking for a coronation or coming-of-age date, in review round 2 (sh <scratch>/run.sh q4b; no rows)
5. English, Swedish, Danish and mul labels and aliases and en/sv/da Wikipedia sitelinks of the 22 monarchs and the three house items (python3 <scratch>/names.py, saved as names.json)
6. Finding the position item
6b. Licence of Wikidata's structured data
queries.query: curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o <scratch>/wikidata-licensing.txt "https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Wikidata:Licensing&action=raw"; grep -o "All structured data.\{0,200\}" <scratch>/wikidata-licensing.txt

queries.purpose: 7. The Royal House's list of monarchs (found with a web search for "kongehuset.dk kongerækken Christian I 1448 Frederik X"), downloaded and reduced to text
8. Lex's article on the Danish royal line (found with a web search for "lex.dk kongerækken danske konger og dronninger liste"), downloaded and reduced to text
9. Lex's terms for articles marked "begrænset genbrug" (a first guess, https://lex.dk/.vilk%C3%A5r, answered 404; the link was then taken from the article page)
10. Wikitext and revision id of the Swedish Wikipedia list of Danish monarchs
11. The article page, for its licence footer
12. Nationalencyklopedin on Frederik X (a web search for "ne.se uppslagsverk Frederik X kung av Danmark" found no NE page; the address was tried directly)
13. Nationalencyklopedin on Kristian IV
14. Nationalencyklopedin's copyright page (address found in the article page's HTML; first read with a web-fetch tool, then downloaded for the exact wording)

15. Wikitext of the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica articles on five Danish kings through the English Wikisource MediaWiki API (first run while authoring, re-run in review round 3; the script calls https://en.wikisource.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=1911+Encyclop%C3%A6dia+Britannica%2F<title>&prop=wikitext%7Crevid&redirects=1&format=json for each title). The article pages only transclude scanned pages (e.g. "Christian IV." revision 12112574: <pages index="EB1911 - Volume 06.djvu" from=292 to=293 …/>, "|contributor=Robert Nisbet Bain").
queries.query: python3 <scratch>/eb1911.py "Christian II." "Christian III." "Christian IV." "Christian VII." "Christian IX."

queries.purpose: 16. The transcribed scan page holding the start of "Christian IV." (vol. 6, p. 276), in review round 3
17. The licence box of the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica on Wikisource
18. Robert Nisbet Bain's Wikidata item, for his dates

rounds.lens: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's monarch and years against Wikidata, the Royal House's list, Lex and the Swedish Wikipedia; the Swedish names against Wikidata sv labels, the Swedish Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin; the current monarch against all of them.
rounds.scope: All 22 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.
rounds.summary: Wikidata, Lex and the Swedish Wikipedia agree on the monarch and the first and last year of all 22 reigns, and the Royal House's list agrees on 19. Its three different figures (Hans, Christian III, Christian IV) are named in those cards' notes (round 3 later took them out of the notes; they remain in the cards' evidence). No Wikidata check was skipped; the builder's checks all pass against live Wikidata. The other findings concern name forms and Wikidata modelling and change no card's facts.

findings.issue: The Royal House's list gives Hans 1482–1513 (heading and timeline); Wikidata (P580 1481), Lex ("1481-1513") and the Swedish Wikipedia ("Kung 21 maj 1481 vid Kristian I:s död") count from his father's death in 1481.
findings.resolution: The card follows the deck's accession convention and three of the four sources: 1481–1513. The note says that the Royal House's list counts from 1482.

findings.issue: The Royal House's page gives Christian III as 1534–1559 in its timeline but "Christian III (1536-1559)" in the entry heading, and an interregnum of 1533–1536; Lex gives the interregnum as 1533–1534 and the reign as 1534–1559, the Swedish Wikipedia "Vald till kung 4 juli 1534", Wikidata P580 1534-07-14.
findings.resolution: Back 1534–1559 (accession by election); the note says the throne was vacant 1533–1534 and that the Royal House's list also gives 1536.

findings.issue: The Royal House's list writes "1588/1596-1648": 1596 is the year he came of age and was crowned (Lex: "Først 8 år senere i 1596 blev han kronet til dansk-norsk konge og dermed regent"; Nationalencyklopedin likewise). Wikidata, Lex's timeline, the Swedish Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin ("kung av Danmark–Norge från 1588") count from 1588.
findings.resolution: Back 1588–1648 by the accession convention (coronations are not used); the note says he became king at ten and that the Royal House's list writes 1588/1596.

findings.issue: On the Royal House's page the entry for Frederik III is headed "Frederik VIII (1648-1670)", evidently a slip; its timeline row reads "Frederik III 1648-1670".
findings.resolution: The years agree with every source; the slip is recorded in the card's evidence.

findings.issue: English usage mixes Frederick and Frederik: Wikidata's English labels are "Frederick I/II/III/V/VI/VII of Denmark" but "Frederik IV of Denmark" (alias "Frederick IV"), "Frederik VIII of Denmark", "Frederik IX of Denmark" and "Frederik X of Denmark"; the English Wikipedia titles are Frederick I–VIII, Frederik IX and Frederik X; the Royal House's English page writes Frederik throughout.
findings.resolution: One stated rule: Frederick for the seven Oldenburg kings, Frederik for the three Glücksburg kings, each form a Wikidata English label or alias of that item (checked by the builder). Explained in the method.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label is "John, King of Denmark" and the Swedish label "Johan II" (his Swedish regnal name); a front "John" or "Johan II" would not be the name under which Danish lists know him.
findings.resolution: Front "Hans" in both languages: the English alias "Hans", the English Wikipedia title "Hans, King of Denmark", the Swedish alias "Hans av Danmark", the Swedish Wikipedia title "Hans (kung)" and the list's "Hans". The Swedish name John II / Johan II is in the note.

findings.issue: Swedish forms: the historical kings are Kristian and Fredrik in Swedish (Wikidata sv labels and aliases, the Swedish Wikipedia, Nationalencyklopedin "Fredrik IX (danska Frederik IX)"), but the present king is Frederik X in Swedish (Wikidata sv label "Frederik X av Danmark", the Swedish Wikipedia, Nationalencyklopedin "Frederik X"); Wikidata also has the Swedish alias "Fredrik X av Danmark".
findings.resolution: The deck follows established Swedish usage for each monarch: Fredrik IX but Frederik X, and Margrethe II (not Margareta). Explained in the method.

findings.issue: Wikidata gives Margrethe II two P53 (family) values: House of Glücksburg (Q155616) and House of Laborde de Monpezat (Q3065853), the family of her husband, Prince Henrik.
findings.resolution: The note names the House of Glücksburg, under which Lex lists her; the builder checks P53 = Q155616. The Laborde de Monpezat value is not used.

findings.issue: Wikidata's P582 for Christian VII is 1808-03-14 but his date of death 1808-03-13, and Wikidata's dates for the reigns before 1700 are converted to the Gregorian calendar (Christian IV 1588-04-14, the Swedish Wikipedia 4 April 1588).
findings.resolution: The cards give years only, on which every source agrees.

findings.issue: Recency: whether Frederik X still reigned on 4 October 2026.
findings.resolution: Confirmed on 4 October 2026 by Wikidata (preferred-rank statement, no end time), the Royal House ("Since 2024"), Lex ("2024-", article last changed 15 September 2026) and Nationalencyklopedin ("kung av Danmark sedan 2024"). The back is "2024–" and the note says "as of October 2026".

findings.issue: The House of Glücksburg has two Wikidata items: Q155616 (the whole house, Swedish label "Schleswig-Holstein-Sonderburg-Glücksburg") and Q111201485 (its Danish branch, Swedish label "huset Glücksburg"); Frederik VIII, Christian X and Frederik IX hold only the second as P53.
findings.resolution: English note "House of Glücksburg" (label of Q155616), Swedish note "Huset Glücksburg" (label of Q111201485, capitalised at the start of the note); each card's P53 check names the item that monarch holds.

rounds.scope: All 22 cards: reign years against a live Wikidata query of every P39 statement for Monarch of Denmark, the Royal House's page fetched afresh, the note facts against Wikidata P569/P570, and a web search for any change of monarch in 2026.
rounds.summary: No factual errors: every holder and every start and end year matches live Wikidata, the Royal House's page reads as the evidence says, and Frederik X still reigns. One optional suggestion, applied: a note on Frederik VIII's card that English also writes Frederick VIII.

findings.issue: The English fronts change from "Frederick VII" to "Frederik VIII" by the deck's house rule (Frederick for Oldenburg, Frederik for Glücksburg), but the English Wikipedia and most English works write "Frederick VIII", so the change can look like a slip and a learner answering "Frederick VIII" sees a different spelling.
findings.resolution: Verified: Wikidata's en label of Q152756 is "Frederik VIII of Denmark" and its enwiki sitelink "Frederick VIII of Denmark" (query 5). The documented rule is kept and the note now says "Also written Frederick VIII in English." / "På engelska skrivs namnet även Frederick VIII.", sourced from the enwiki sitelink in the card's Wikidata evidence.

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent language, translation and language tags reviewer
rounds.scope: All 22 cards, the title, the description and the keywords: English and Swedish name forms against live Wikidata labels, aliases and sitelinks and Nationalencyklopedin, Swedish idiom and conventions, language tags and back uniqueness.
rounds.summary: No language errors; the Swedish name forms, lower-case conventions, zxx backs and bidirectional study all hold. Three minor findings, all resolved: the unclear 1536 sentence and the "skriver 1588/1596" sentence were removed together with the other Royal House sentences (see round 3), Christian IV's note now says he came of age in 1596, and Frederik VIII's note gives the English spelling Frederick VIII.

findings.issue: The note's sentence "The Royal House's list also gives 1536." / "Det danska kungahusets lista anger även 1536." does not say what 1536 is.
findings.resolution: Verified: on the Royal House's page 1536 is the start year in the entry heading "Christian III (1536-1559)" and the end of its interregnum. The sentence was removed rather than reworded, as part of the round-3 licensing fix that takes the Royal House's figures out of the notes; the note now reads "House of Oldenburg. Son of Frederick I; the throne was vacant from 1533 to 1534." / "Huset Oldenburg. Son till Fredrik I; tronen stod tom 1533–1534." The 1536 figure stays in the card's evidence and round 0.
